jess (platform-pm): Heads-up: customer X in prod private VPC asked for self-service burst policies + per-key quotas. We need a proposal for how enforcement works between the private control plane and the on-prem agent.
liam (eng): quick notes: must support per-org and per-api-key limits, plus short bursts (leaky bucket). enforcement ideally local to avoid network hop.
anika (eng-platform): Agreed. two modes: 
- controller-managed: control plane pushes policy to agent (private control plane in customer's VPC)
- customer-managed: customer uploads JSON policy only, agent enforces locally, control plane is just for telemetry and audit
kevin (sre): Important: telemetry only is fine, but we need a safety fallback if agent misbehaves. If agent fails to enforce, should we default to allowing or denying?
jess (platform-pm): Safety-first: default deny would break customer apps. proposal: fail-open for short window + alert + control-plane soft-throttle until agent back.
liam (eng): Implementation detail: policy format should include: window, tokens, burst_capacity, scope (org|key), priority, and optional weight. Example: 
```json
{
  "scope": "api_key",
  "id": "k_live_123",
  "limit": 120,
  "per_seconds": 60,
  "burst": 300,
  "algorithm": "leaky_bucket"
}
```
anika (eng-platform): UX: console should let customers preview effective RPS and estimated cost impact based on recent telemetry. Also a quick sanity-check that catches rules that are too tight.
kevin (sre): Also add rollout controls: staged activation (10% keys -> 50% -> 100%) and canary by org. Can't have a single bad policy kill everything.
jess (platform-pm): Telemetry contract idea: agent emits events to control plane (or to customer telemetry) with event types: quota.check, quota.decision, quota.eviction. Must include policy_id, scope, observed_tokens, decision (allow|reject|throttle), reason, and timestamp.
liam (eng): Example minimum telemetry payload: 
```json
{"event":"quota.decision","policy_id":"p-789","scope":"org_42","key":"k_live_123","decision":"throttle","used":310,"burst":300,"limit":120,"window_s":60}
```
anika (eng-platform): For private deployments we need an opt-in telemetry path: many customers want control-plane offline. So agent should buffer telemetry and either push to customer-managed endpoint or hold for on-prem collection. Also add sampling for high-volume events.
kevin (sre): Enforcement algorithm details: leaky bucket at request arrival, but also support token-bucket so customers can buy bursts. We should expose which algorithm in UI.
liam (eng): API contract for customers who want to manage policies via API (self-serve): 
POST /v1/private/policies -> validate -> push to agent -> return applied: {applied:true, errors:[], preview:{expected_rps: 45}}
If agent unreachable, allow "staged_apply": true which uploads policy to control plane and marks it PENDING until agent pulls it.
jess (platform-pm): Edge case: multiple policies per-scope. We need deterministic merge: most-restrictive wins for rejects, most-permissive for bursts? or explicit precedence field. Thoughts?
anika (eng-platform): explicit precedence is better. allow combining via "rules" array with priority. avoid magic.
liam (eng): Also discuss counters: local agent maintains per-key counters in-memory and periodically checkpoints to disk to survive restarts. For long windows we need persistent counts or centralization.
kevin (sre): Persistance: use embedded RocksDB on agent, compacting TTL for counters to avoid unbounded growth.
jess (platform-pm): UX stuff again: in console show active policies, pending sync status, last_seen_agent_timestamp, and a "simulate" button to run your rule against last 24h traffic to show rejects.
anika (eng-platform): For RBAC: in private deployments only org-admins should manage policies. Console role mapping: org_owner + quota_admin. Also add audit log entries for every policy change.
liam (eng): Backwards compatibility: existing hosted policy API should still work; convert to new schema when syncing to private agents. write a migration layer in controller.
kevin (sre): Tests: chaos test where agent loses connectivity for 5 mins, see fail-open behavior, verify alerts and rollback. Also golden metrics: false_reject_rate < 0.1% in steady-state.
jess (platform-pm): Action items: 
1) liam + anika draft API + on-disk schema and sample policy JSON (ETA Tue)
2) kevin produce SRE runbook + chaos test plans (ETA Wed)
3) design mockups for console preview & simulate (assign to design after mockups)
I'll set a short RFC doc and link here.
devops-bot: Created ticket INF-4723 for "Private VPC: customer-managed rate controls + agent enforcement" assigned to liam, anika. Due 2026-03-24 :calendar: 
liam (eng): ack, starting on schema now.
anika (eng-platform): Quick question: do we want per-route quotas too or keep it per-key/org for v1?
jess (platform-pm): Start with per-org & per-key for v1. per-route can be v2 once infra is stable.
kevin (sre): +1.
liam (eng): I'll push a tiny PoC agent plugin in the private-agent repo and share logs in this thread when ready.
